ON THE 6 th OF AUGUST, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 6073 of 2024  VINOD KUMAR HAROR  Versus  SHEIKH CHANDU PASHA @ CHAIN BASHA AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Anshul Shrivastava, learned counsel for the app  Shri P.K.Gupta with Shri Bhashkar Agrawal, learned c  respondent No.3.
 ORDER
The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 7.10.2023 passed in Claim Case No.61/2021 challenging the quantum of compensation.
The issue regarding accident and liability of Insurance Company are not under dispute.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 18.3.2020 at around 6.00 AM appellant was going on his vehicle i.e. truck No.MP-09-HH-8568 from Vishakhapattanam to Chhitaurgarh (Rajasthan).

When he reached near Pindiprolu, Trumalayapalem District Khammam, respondent No.1 came driving Traula No.AP-16-TY-3692 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the vehicle of appellant,
because of which appellant sustained injuries.

2.1 The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20926 2 MA-6073-2024 Vehicles Act for the injuries sustained by him claiming compensation.

sentences.text: The claims Tribunal after evaluation of the evidence on record awarded total sum of Rs.19,76,742/- to the appellant.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that while assessing income the claims Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head of future prospects.

he submits that at the time of accident appellant was 52 years of age as per conclusion of the claims Tribunal in para 21 of the award, thus 25% should be added in income of the appellant for future prospects.

4. sentences.text: very higher side.
He submits that the award of compensation is just and proper.
Thus, no interference is warranted.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.
6.
It is seen that claims Tribunal in para 21 of the award has itself concluded that the appellant-injured was 42 years of age at the time of accident.
It has further been recorded by the claims Tribunal that appellant was earning Rs.9,000/- per month and he has not been treated as salaried person.

In view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, the addition of 25% in the income of the injured has to be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the amount of compensation for permanent disability would change to Rs.16,06,500/- and the total compensation would now come to Rs.22,98,042/-.

The claims Tribunal has already awarded the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20926 3 MA-6073-2024 of Rs.19,76,742/-.
Thus, now the appellant is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,21,300/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.

7. It is seen from the award that though in para 26 interest @ 6% per annum has been awarded from the date of filing of claim application before the claims Tribunal, but in para 28(i) the interest applied from the date of award, it appears to be error due to oversight.
Thus, it is clarified that the appellant is entitled for the interest on the entire amount including enhanced amount from the date of filing claim application till its payment.
8. With the aforesaid, the present appeal is partly allowed and disposed off.
